headline: New Zealand Dollar Falls to 17-Year Low Against US Dollar Amid Global Market Pressure
summary: The New Zealand dollar slumped to its lowest level against the US dollar since the 2009 Global Financial Crisis, driven by global share market volatility and broader currency weakness.
why: The New Zealand dollar is a major export-driven Asia-Pacific currency sensitive to global risk appetite and commodity trade sentiment.

impacts.name: New Zealand Dollar
impacts.why: Global equity market turbulence pressured risk-sensitive currencies, dragging the NZD to 17-year lows.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Broad weakness across global equity markets exacerbated depreciation in the New Zealand dollar.
